title: [recoverability] the fleet's notes folder (/var/tmp/spawn/sync) in the existing encrypted R2 bundle: full weekly, increments by size, mtime and sha256, a manifest inside, the files scanned for credential values first (a hit or a blind place drops the part), read only
prompt:
Spawn, objective 216 [recoverability] (owner t489u, candidate A step 3; lead-mac's proposal sync/proposal-sync-backup-hook.md of 2026-11-17 18:1x; lead's approvals of 2026-11-17; author rev-i): the fleet's notes folder goes into the existing encrypted R2 bundle, scanned for credential values first, read only.

Base: live main 564ea184.

The problem: /var/tmp/spawn/sync (about 212 MB, 10,601 files: seals, review texts, ready marks, gate state, cc-rules, inboxes, queue, roadmap) is in no backup and no drill. The hourly dump holds the event log; the daily bundle holds the mission repos and the transcript archive only (crates/spawn-cli/src/backup.rs, fn bundle).

What changes:
(1) `spawn backup bundle` takes one more source when SPAWN_BACKUP_SYNC_DIR is set. Unset: no record field, no bundle entry, no file; the bundle is as before.
(2) Set: the folder is walked read only. Regular files are taken; a symbolic link or special file is listed in `skipped`, never followed. Each file is hashed, copied, re-hashed and re-statted; a file that changed is read again once, then listed in `changed_during_read` and left out of the manifest, never mixed.
(3) Inside the bundle: sync/files (the full: every file; an increment: the files whose size, mtime or sha256 differ from the base bundle's manifest) and sync/manifest.json (every file's path, size, mtime_ms, mode, sha256; `taken`, `removed`, `skipped`, `changed_during_read`). The bundle's manifest.json says where they are, or that the part was refused.
(4) The base manifest: a local copy (<workspace root>/.backup-sync-manifest.json) written after each stored bundle that holds the part, trusted only when its sha256 equals the base record's sync.manifest_sha256 and that record stored its bundle; otherwise the run takes every file and says `base_manifest: \"unusable: <why>\"`.
(5) The value scan, the lead's condition: before the tar, the staged files go through SPAWN_BACKUP_SYNC_SCAN (default /usr/local/lib/spawn/redact/secret-scan-files.py, which loads secret-values.py), run as `python3 -I <tool> <staged dir>`, stderr dropped, its output read for places only. Exit 0 keeps the part. Exit 1 (a value or key block) drops it. Exit 3 keeps it only when every place not seen into was searched raw (binary (NUL bytes), not UTF-8 text, high entropy), and the record names those places; any other unseen reason drops it. Exit 2, any other code, a kill or a missing tool drops it. A dropped part takes nothing else with it: the transcripts and repos are stored as before.
(6) The backup.bundled record gains `sync`: {dir, kind full|incremental, base_manifest, files, bytes, taken, taken_bytes, removed, skipped, changed_during_read, manifest_sha256, scan: {exit, unseen: [{path, why}]} | null} or {dir, refused}. Counts and a hash, never the file list, a value or the path of a hit.
(7) deploy/systemd/spawn-backup-bundle.service: Environment=SPAWN_BACKUP_SYNC_DIR=/var/tmp/spawn/sync (a non-secret line, not in spawn.env). The six scenarios that run the bundle unit (149, 186, 198, 199, 200, 203) leave that line out of their unit runs, so none reads live sync/.
(8) lead-mac's 19:07 risks: with the folder set, the bundle's scratch (the staged files, the tar, its compressed, encrypted and decrypted-back copies: about 640 MB for a full) is a hidden directory in the workspace root, on disk beside the lock, never in TMPDIR (/tmp is memory on this host); unset, it stays where it was. A file or directory the run cannot read drops the sync/ part with the reason naming it, as a scan refusal does; nothing else fails.

R2 budget: unchanged; the part is inside the one archive, under the existing SPAWN_BACKUP_R2_LIMIT_MB check.

What stays as it is: the dump, keys, bucket, lock, retention, the session backup, the restore drill (217 adds the sync/ drill after 216 lands). Nothing is ever written to or cleaned in the notes folder.
(9) A bundle's PUT is given 600 s plus its size at 100 KB/s (the last max-time of its curl config), a backstop sized to the object, not a speed relied on. GETs are not changed here: lead-mac's owner-dlfix makes the shared get_object_bytes resume a cut transfer with Range, cut a stall and retry; 216 and 217 use that path (lead-mac 20:0x, owner t494u). Increments carry only the folder's new or changed files (about 20 MB of 214 MB changed in the last day, 2026-11-17), so a typical daily bundle is not a full-size object; the weekly full is (about 229 MB). The manifest inside a bundle is the files as that run read them (each hashed, copied and re-hashed); 217's drill compares with it, never with the live folder's moving hashes, and never restores onto sync/.

Memory: the sync part hashes and copies in 64 KiB reads and never holds a file whole; its manifest (one entry per file, about 2 MB for 10,600 files) is the largest thing it keeps in memory. The scan is its own process: over the live folder (10,793 files, 2026-11-17 19:2x) it took 31 s and at most 23 MB resident, exit 3 with all 331 unseen places searched raw (329 binary, 2 not UTF-8), so the part is kept. The unit sets no MemoryMax, and none is added.

Files: crates/spawn-cli/src/backup/sync_dir.rs (new), crates/spawn-cli/src/backup.rs; owner: deploy/systemd/spawn-backup-bundle.service, deploy/systemd/README.md, rsi/scenarios/149.sh, 186.sh, 198.sh, 199.sh, 200.sh, 203.sh, rsi/scenarios/216.sh, rsi/backlog/216.json.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/216.sh, black box on its own database, scratch HOME and a scratch notes folder, against the R2 stand-in, with a stand-in scan that answers as the real one does: (1) a full bundle holds every file and the manifest whose sha256 the record names, the symbolic link skipped and the binary file named as not seen into; (2) an increment after a change, an add and a remove holds those 2 files and names the removed one; (3) a credential value, (4) a place not seen into, (5) a missing scan tool, (5b) an unreadable file (named) each drop the part while the rest is stored; the bundle's tar packs a folder in the workspace root, not TMPDIR (a logging tar first in PATH); (6) unset gives no sync part; (7) the bundle unit, run as systemd runs it, takes the notes folder; (8) no run changes the folder or leaves scratch in the workspace, and no secret is in any output or record. On live main 564ea184 216.sh exits 1 at (1): the record has no sync part. The exit-3 rules, the base-manifest trust and a file whose bytes are equal with a new mtime are covered by the unit tests in sync_dir.rs.

Verified by: the gate runs 216.sh. Live, the next daily bundle's record names a sync part, and its bundle holds the notes folder.
